# API stability and test coverage

Two numbers that say how much of Mirage is promised and how much of it the Node checks execute, and the rule for
moving a name from *experimental* to *stable*. Both are measured by scripts in this repository; neither gates CI.

## How much is stable

`npm run stability` imports each package's entry point and classes every exported name by the
[api.md](api.md) row that describes it (`-- --write` rewrites the block below). 1.0.0:

<!-- generated by scripts/api-stability.mjs: do not edit by hand -->
| package | exports | stable | experimental | not in a row | stable share | subpaths |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `@mirage/core` | 112 | 17 | 95 | 0 | 15 % | 44 |
| `@mirage/world` | 11 | 7 | 4 | 0 | 64 % | 13 |
| `@mirage/play` | 73 | 5 | 68 | 0 | 7 % | 18 |
| `@mirage/game` | 50 | 8 | 42 | 0 | 16 % | 24 |
| `@mirage/net` | 21 | 0 | 21 | 0 | 0 % | 4 |
| `@mirage/editor` | 19 | 0 | 19 | 0 | 0 % | 3 |
| **all** | **286** | **37** | **249** | **0** | **13 %** | 106 |
<!-- end generated -->

Read it as: about one export in six carries the 1.0 promise. That is deliberate. The stable set is what a world
needs to be built, walked, tested and shipped (the renderer, `geom`, the procedural materials, the world protocol,
`createPlay`, `createGame`, input, physics, audio), and it is what the examples are written against. The
experimental set is the 2026 feature work (lighting, post, VFX, animation, UI, big worlds, import / export, XR and
all of `@mirage/net`): shipped, documented and checked, but with months rather than years of use behind it.

Subpaths are part of the surface too: each `package.json` lists its importable paths under `exports`, a path that
is not listed cannot be imported, and removing one is a breaking change. A subpath has the stability of the names
it exports.

## What the words mean

| | stable | experimental |
|---|---|---|
| a breaking change (a removed or renamed name, a changed argument or return shape, a changed default that alters output) | major release only, with a deprecation in a minor before it where that is possible | any minor release, listed under **Changes in behaviour** in the CHANGELOG |
| rendered output of unchanged calls | fixed within a major: the golden stills are the test | may change in a minor, with before / after stills in the guide |
| declarations (`.d.ts`) | complete, checked against the runtime exports in `npm test` | the same check; shapes may be loose (`object`) |

Anything not in a row of [api.md](api.md) (internal modules, `_`-prefixed fields, the files under `src/` that no
`exports` entry names) is not API at all.

## Promoting a name to stable

A name moves from experimental to stable in a minor release when all of these hold; the pull request that moves
it says where each can be seen.

1. **Two minor releases without a breaking change** to its signature, defaults or output.
2. **Used by something that ships**: at least one example or demo in `examples/` uses it through the public
   import path, and that example has a playtest that would fail if it broke.
3. **Checked without a GPU and with one**: a Node check for its logic and, where it draws, a browser check with
   stills. Its own source file is above the repository's coverage figure below, or the pull request says why the
   uncovered part cannot run in Node.
4. **Lifecycle closed**: everything it creates is released by its `dispose()` or by the world's, shown by
   `packages/tools/dispose-check.mjs` or a check like it ([LIFECYCLE.md](LIFECYCLE.md)).
5. **Documented as it is**: an [api.md](api.md) row, a guide with measured numbers, declarations with no `any` in
   the arguments, and diagnostics for the mistakes people make with it ([diagnostics.md](diagnostics.md)).
6. **The owner agrees.** Stability is a promise somebody has to keep.

Promote the smallest thing that is useful: a function with three of its options, not a module with thirty. An
option can stay experimental inside a stable function when its row says so.

Going the other way (stable to experimental, or removal) is a major release. An experimental name that has had
no user and no change for two minor releases is a candidate for removal, not for promotion.

## Coverage of the Node checks

`npm run coverage` runs `npm test` with `NODE_V8_COVERAGE` (V8's own coverage, built into Node: no dependency)
and aggregates the raw ranges over every file in `packages/*/src` (`scripts/coverage.mjs` explains the counting;
`--files` lists each file). A file no Node check loads counts as zero.

<!-- coverage -->
Measured 2026-11-11 on Node 22.23.1 (macOS), one run of `npm test`:

| package | files (loaded) | characters run | lines run | functions run (in loaded files) |
| `@mirage/core` | 55 (53) | 45.4 % | 50.1 % of 9745 | 66.4 % of 670 |
| `@mirage/editor` | 10 (6) | 19.7 % | 23.3 % of 1877 | 71.5 % of 144 |
| `@mirage/game` | 30 (30) | 57.7 % | 65.6 % of 5703 | 72.3 % of 896 |
| `@mirage/net` | 16 (16) | 82.2 % | 90.6 % of 1774 | 84.2 % of 341 |
| `@mirage/play` | 31 (31) | 58.8 % | 63.4 % of 5369 | 84.6 % of 591 |
| `@mirage/tools` | 56 (19) | 25.4 % | 26.6 % of 6434 | 86.2 % of 326 |
| `@mirage/world` | 12 (12) | 84.0 % | 88.9 % of 1445 | 89.2 % of 195 |
| **all** | 210 (167) | 46.8 % | 52.8 % of 32347 | 77.1 % of 3163 |
<!-- end coverage -->

About half of the lines (52.8 % of 32 347) run in the Node checks. "Loaded" is the number of files any check
imported; most of `@mirage/tools` is command-line entry points and browser drivers that only the browser checks
start.

What the number is not: it is the Node half. The browser checks (`npm run test:e2e`, the software-GL job, the
per-feature `*.check.mjs` that open Chrome) run the shaders, the WebGL paths and the DOM code, and are not counted
here, so files that are mostly GLSL strings or renderer calls read low for a reason. Use `--files` to find logic
that could be checked in Node and is not; do not chase the total.
